title: Adversarial Constrained Bidding via Minimax Regret Optimization with Causality-Aware Reinforcement Learning

problem.claim: Constrained bidding strategies must optimize advertising objectives under spending constraints in repeated, potentially adversarial online auctions without assuming knowledge of adversarial factors.

gap.claim: Existing constrained-bidding approaches typically rely on i.i.d. train and test conditions, which conflict with the adversarial nature of online advertising markets.

contributions.claim: MiRO interleaves a teacher that finds adversarial environments for tutoring with a learner that meta-learns its policy over a distribution of environments.
MiROCL improves MiRO through a causality-aware policy that distills knowledge from expert demonstrations.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on industrial and synthetic data are reported to show that MiROCL outperforms prior methods by over 30%.

narrative_sequence.summary: Online advertising uses repeated auctions in which agents optimize long-term advertiser utility under diverse objectives and spending constraints.
Standard constrained-bidding methods assume i.i.d. train and test conditions despite adversarial market participants.
The work aligns training environments with potential test distributions while minimizing policy regret through MiRO.
MiROCL adds expert demonstrations and causality-aware policy design to distill expert knowledge.
The authors report improvements over prior methods on industrial and synthetic data.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the exact bidding objectives, spending constraints, adversarial factors, or environment distribution.
The abstract does not provide dataset sizes, baselines, evaluation metrics, or statistical details behind the reported improvement.
The abstract does not describe the causality-aware policy architecture or the expert demonstrations.
